results.evidence: results/formal/table1/metrics.csv and results/formal/table1/summary.json provide per-trial and mean elapsed_seconds for all four configurations. Mean CPU times (time_mean_seconds from summary.json): Peppers BSNR=30: APIRL1-AM=8.5710s vs PIRL1-AM=12.9102s (APIRL1 faster ✅); Cameraman BSNR=30: APIRL1-AM=3.4759s vs PIRL1-AM=3.4354s (APIRL1 SLOWER ❌); Peppers BSNR=20: APIRL1-AM=5.9501s vs PIRL1-AM=6.7038s (APIRL1 faster ✅); Cameraman BSNR=20: APIRL1-AM=2.2112s vs PIRL1-AM=2.2059s (APIRL1 SLOWER ❌). Only 2 of 4 cases satisfy the claim; the aggregation rule requires at least 4 of 4.
results.note: The Cameraman configurations show APIRL1-AM taking slightly more CPU time than PIRL1-AM on average, contradicting the claim. Notably, the summary.json "paper_table" section shows different (scaled?) times where APIRL1-AM appears faster for Cameraman, but the actual trial data and time_mean_seconds in the "summary" section consistently show PIRL1-AM is faster for Cameraman at both BSNR levels.
